key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Pilate’s authority and brutal punishment.
key_decisions.before: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.
key_decisions.after: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves repeated mockery and physical abuse.
key_decisions.before: They kept coming up to him and saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!” and slapping him.
key_decisions.after: They kept coming up to him and saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!” And they slapped him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: They came up to him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they struck him with their hands.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves law, death claim, and stated charge.
key_decisions.before: The Jewish leaders answered, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die because he made himself God’s Son.”
key_decisions.after: The Judean leaders answered him, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die because he made himself the Son of God.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die, because he has made himself the Son of God.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves derivative authority, above ambiguity, causal conclusion, handover, and comparative guilt.
key_decisions.before: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has greater sin.”
key_decisions.after: Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore, the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority over me unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps festival timing, approximate sixth hour, audience, and title.
key_decisions.before: It was the day of Preparation for Passover, about the sixth hour. Pilate said to the Jewish leaders, “Look—your king!”
key_decisions.after: It was the day of preparation for Passover, about noon. Pilate told the Judean leaders, “Here is your king!”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now it was the day of Preparation for the Passover, and it was about noon. He said to the Jews, “Here is your king.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves repeated rejection, crucifixion demand, Pilate’s question, and chief priests’ declaration.
key_decisions.before: They shouted, “Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him!” Pilate asked, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”
key_decisions.after: They shouted, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate asked them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps broad readership, geographic reason, and three languages.
key_decisions.before: Many Jewish people read this notice because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
key_decisions.after: Many Jewish people read this notice because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. It was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Many of the Jews read this inscription, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the women’s presence and named relationships without resolving whether two descriptions overlap.
key_decisions.before: Standing near Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
key_decisions.after: Standing near Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Jesus’ knowledge, completion, spoken thirst, and fulfillment purpose.
key_decisions.before: After this, Jesus knew that everything had now been completed. So that Scripture might be fulfilled, he said, “I am thirsty.”
key_decisions.after: After this, knowing that everything was now completed, Jesus said, “I am thirsty,” so that Scripture would be fulfilled.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: After this, Jesus, knowing that all was now finished, said, in order to fulfill the scripture, “I am thirsty.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps reception, completed work, bodily movement, and voluntary-sounding death idiom.
key_decisions.before: When Jesus received the sour wine, he said, “It is completed.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
key_decisions.after: After receiving the sour wine, Jesus said, “It is completed.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and handed over his spirit.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves timing, bodies, crosses, special Sabbath, request, and violent procedure.
key_decisions.before: Because it was Preparation Day, the Jewish leaders did not want the bodies to remain on the crosses during the Sabbath—because that Sabbath was a great day—so they asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies taken away.
key_decisions.after: Because it was the day of preparation, the Judean leaders did not want the bodies to remain on the crosses during the Sabbath—especially since that Sabbath was a great day. So they asked Pilate to have the men’s legs broken and the bodies removed.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Since it was the day of Preparation, and so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath —for that Sabbath was a great day— the Jews asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and the bodies taken away.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps spear wound, body side, immediacy, blood, and water.
key_decisions.before: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
key_decisions.after: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves eyewitness, repeated truth claim, knowledge, and purpose.
key_decisions.before: The one who saw this has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows he is telling the truth so that you also may trust.
key_decisions.after: The one who saw this has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, so that you also may believe.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: The one who saw this has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves identity, prior night visit, materials, and large approximate weight.
key_decisions.before: Nicodemus, the man who had first come to Jesus at night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about a hundred pounds.
key_decisions.after: Nicodemus, who had first come to Jesus at night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about a hundred Roman pounds.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to Jesus by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
